headline: A World Bank report cites a Chinese study in which students using AI got better homework scores but worse exam results.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a useful education finding, but from a study that is not yet peer-reviewed.
importance_line: Students and teachers get early evidence that AI can help homework while weakening learning, but the study is not yet peer-reviewed and the same report says AI tutoring can help when teachers guide it.
summary: The Times of India reports that the World Bank's World Development Report 2026 cites a study of Chinese students in classes 7 to 12 in which homework scores rose 18% six months after they first used AI, while monthly in-class exam scores fell 20%. The report says the study is not yet peer-reviewed, and notes that AI tutoring in other experiments gave learning gains of at least half a year of schooling when it supported teachers.
notes: NewsBytes original blocked and is a copy; url is the Times of India article where the text was read.
